head: 887f17e
phantoms_i_tried: nested HTML comment <!-- <!-- --> then grid (correctly True: grid is after a closed comment)
fence opened, closing fence inside a comment (correctly False: fail-closed)
blockquote markdown > | a | b | (correctly False: '>' becomes a non-separator cell)
2-space / 3-space list-indented table (True: these ARE real GFM tables)
separator with a single trailing space (True: real grid)
zero-width space / RTL mark in header cells (True: real grid with invisible chars)

findings.what: Raw HTML blocks are not stripped, so a markdown table inside <pre>/<div>/<code>/<script>/<style>/<blockquote> ships as a phantom over the D3 marker. The stripping sequence handles HTML comments, fenced code, and 4-space/tab indented code, but not CommonMark's raw-HTML block (type 6), which is the same 'code sample, not a reading' class the author just closed three times.
findings.why:
Driven through _winning_page_output with model_text = '
| a | b |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |
' and rejection_class='judge_only': the page ships WARNING with the marker fully suppressed and the 'kept a model reading' note present. In GFM a table inside a raw HTML block is NOT rendered as a table, so this is a syntax-level phantom, not a provenance one. It directly falsifies the round-5 central claim that 'the remaining failure class is provenance, not syntax' — a markdown parser CAN see that 
 content is not a table. The fix is one more stripping pass (blank lines inside raw-HTML block tags) plus corpus + page-level cases.

what_i_tried_to_break: Built 14 adversarial inputs and drove the strict predicate directly, then the three that returned True through the full _winning_page_output path. The raw-HTML-block family (<pre>, <div>, <code>, <script>, <style>, <blockquote>) all return True at the predicate and all ship WARNING with the marker suppressed at page level. Everything else I tried either fails closed (nested comments, fence-closed-in-comment, blockquote markdown, BOM) or is a genuine GFM table (2-3 space list indent, trailing-space separator, CRLF, zero-width/RTL marks). Re-ran the baseline at f9f16b9 in a throwaway worktree: the three round-5 phantoms return True there (ship) and False at 887f17e, confirming non-vacuity; removed the worktree after. find_table_blocks is byte-identical between 4c18ef2 and 887f17e. The 51-case corpus is read back from tests.STRICT_GRID_CASES and re-executed via test_the_strict_predicate_on_its_own_terms, so it cannot drift from the code. The three round-5 phantoms are asserted at page level through _winning_page_output (test_the_reviewers_phantoms_do_not_suppress_the_marker), but the raw-HTML-block phantom is asserted nowhere.
